Definition: Claiming something is true or good because many people are joining in or doing it right now. Popular momentum is treated as proof.
Example: An advert urges, 'Everyone is switching to this phone — do not be left behind,' without comparing the phones themselves.
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone says, 'This new spiritual trend is everywhere online, so it must be true and good for you,' based on how fast it is spreading.
HowToRespond: Slow the momentum kindly: 'It is understandable to notice what is trending. Could we ask whether it is true and wise, apart from how popular it feels right now?'
